minor_characters.name: Mrs. Smith of Allenham
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Willoughby’s wealthy relation at Allenham whose discovery of his misconduct leads to his disinheritance; referenced in several conversations and as the unseen owner of Allenham.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her function can be folded into a brief mention of Willoughby’s loss of fortune without keeping her as a character.

minor_characters.name: Miss Morton (and Lady Morton)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The titled heiress repeatedly floated as Edward’s prudent match and used by Fanny and Mrs. Ferrars as a foil; never appears on page.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She serves only as a counterfactual fiancée and can be omitted without affecting the main plot or themes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Pratt
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Lucy Steele’s uncle and schoolmaster near Plymouth, cited only to explain how Lucy and Edward first met.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Edward’s past entanglement with Lucy can be conveyed without naming the uncle or his school.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Ellison
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Gossiping acquaintance connected to Miss Grey’s guardianship who relays London tidings at a party.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her sole purpose is to pass on second-hand news that can be summarized in narration.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Harris
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The apothecary who attends Marianne’s fever at Cleveland and gives periodic prognoses.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Medical attendants are procedural detail; Marianne’s grave illness and recovery can be shown without naming him.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Donavan
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A London physician summoned during Fanny Dashwood’s theatrics and later mentioned around Charlotte Palmer’s confinement.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He has no bearing on the protagonists’ choices or arcs and can be elided.

minor_characters.name: Dr. Davies
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Comic object of Anne Steele’s flirtation in London/Kensington anecdotes.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A light comic aside that does not inform the central plot or themes.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Taylor
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A London acquaintance used in party small talk and to seed minor gossip.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Expendable society color that does not affect outcomes.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Richardson
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Casual acquaintance who escorts the Steeles in the Kensington Gardens scene.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A passing facilitator in a gossip vignette that can be excised.

minor_characters.name: The Careys and the Whitakers
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Barton Park invitees who bulk out dinner tables and picnics.
minor_characters.reason_removable: They are unnamed social furniture whose presence does not alter any decision or reveal interiority.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Rose and Mr. Simpson
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Names dropped in Anne Steele’s chatter about ‘smart beaux’ in Exeter.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Pure background color; removing them loses nothing.

minor_characters.name: Thomas (the Dashwoods’ footman) and Betty (a maid)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named servants who carry notes and news and fetch doctors.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their named identities are unnecessary; errands can be summarized or reassigned generically.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Burgess
minor_characters.appearances_summary: An Exeter acquaintance with whom Anne Steele proposes to stay after Lucy elopes.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one-line haven for a side character that doesn’t touch the main story.

minor_characters.name: Lady Middleton’s children (Annamaria, William, etc.)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Repeatedly exhibited for small talk and comic misrule during visits.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their named antics can be dropped without affecting plot, themes, or character arcs.

minor_characters.name: Lord Courtland
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A name used in Robert Ferrars’s brag about giving ‘advice’ on cottage plans.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A throwaway boast that can be cut with no loss.

subplots.name: The aborted Whitwell excursion and party logistics
subplots.reason_removable: The cancelled outing and guest wrangling add bustle but do not advance the central arcs beyond what a line about Brandon’s sudden departure already provides.

subplots.name: Robert Ferrars’s toothpick-case and haberdashery vignette
subplots.reason_removable: A comic set-piece that introduces his vanity can be replaced by brief narration when he reappears meaningfully later.

subplots.name: Prolonged Middleton/Palmer salon episodes in London
subplots.reason_removable: The card parties, musical evenings, and guest lists chiefly pad the London milieu; the one essential scene—Mrs. Ferrars’s snobbery toward Elinor—can be kept without the surrounding filler.

subplots.name: Kensington Gardens gossip outing with the Steeles
subplots.reason_removable: A second, duplicative round of Lucy/Anne chatter that can be compressed into narration after Lucy’s initial revelation.

subplots.name: The Palmers’ comic marriage and baby-confinement business
subplots.reason_removable: Their bickering and Charlotte’s confinement provide tone but Cleveland’s role in Marianne’s crisis does not require this extended comic business.

subplots.name: Edward’s mysterious ring (lock of hair) mini-mystery
subplots.reason_removable: Elinor’s deduction via the ring is an extra clue to Lucy’s engagement that can be omitted once Lucy discloses it herself.

subplots.name: John Dashwood’s greenhouse and Norland improvement plans
subplots.reason_removable: His petty grand projects satirize him but do not alter the story’s course.

subplots.name: Margaret’s teasing about Elinor’s secret ‘F.’
subplots.reason_removable: A running joke that neither changes decisions nor reveals anything not shown more clearly elsewhere.

digressions.topic: Detailed architectural and room-by-room description of Barton Cottage
digressions.reason_removable: A scenic inventory that can be condensed to a sentence without affecting plot or character.

digressions.topic: General essayistic portrait of Sir John as sportsman and Lady Middleton as mother, with social calendar taxonomy
digressions.reason_removable: A satiric character sketch that can be summarized briefly once their roles are established.

digressions.topic: Fanny Dashwood’s extended diatribe against annuities and servants’ pensions
digressions.reason_removable: The minutiae of her ‘annuity abhorrence’ can be trimmed once their stinginess and its consequence are clear.

digressions.topic: Taste debate on the picturesque (crooked trees, watch-towers, banditti)
digressions.reason_removable: An essay in miniature contrasting temperaments that can be alluded to without the full disquisition.

digressions.topic: Catalogue of private balls, water parties, and Lady Middleton’s invariability
digressions.reason_removable: Scene-setting that reads like social taxonomy and can be compressed without loss.

digressions.topic: Robert Ferrars’s cottage-ornament sermon and plans for Grecian temples and shrubberies
digressions.reason_removable: A comic lecture on taste that delays the plot and can be cut once his vanity is established.
